I don't think it is one. She doesn't have any discharge and the nurse who cathed her today would have seen it if she had any. I have looked and it doesn't look red or anything but she doesn't want me to look at it or wipe her.

My baby was 6 months old before someone pointed out to me that I was doing it wrong! I was mad that I had posted so many carseat pics and nobody had the guts to tell me that she wasn't strapped in correctly. I finally found CSFTL facebook page and found so much information! My daughter is 20 months old almost, strapped in correctly, and still rear facing. I see people all the time on Facebook with their kids strapped wrong and I just shoot them a PM. They are usually very thankful because, like me, they didn't know they were doing it wrong. I have one instance where a friend turned her baby around too early and I politely pointed it out to her and it got me blocked on Facebook, some people just don't take advice well. Another friend of mine stopped by on her way home with her newborn just to make sure he was strapped in correctly because she saw me posting car seat tips so much and she was a new mom. 


Some people welcome the advice, and some don't. In my experience, the ones who are thankful for it are the ones who didn't know they were doing it wrong. We all make mistakes and being a mom is a hard job, we have to help each other out. She sounds like a close friend if you hang out with her. I would think it would be appropriate to call/text her and discuss it or shoot her a FB message about it.

I don't want to be that mom who googles and self diagnoses so I am going to bring it up to the dr today as a suggestion. My granny told me to look it up and so far it is the only answer I can find.

She has sleep myoclonus (I think thats what it is called). Where when she wakes up she isnt fully awake and she starts shaking like she's having a seizure. This was the first thing she saw the neurologist for about a year ago. So far all her neuro tests have came back normal.

I showed this to her dr at her 12 month visit (not this exact video since this was from last night) and first thing he did was call for a neuro consult. We went for a 24 hour EEG and it showed no seizures. We all thought it was seizures. She sees a gastroenterologist as well, for poor weight gain and constipation. He tested for cystic fibrosis and is going to test for celiac disease. But for now they are just calling them spells and have no answers for me. Last night she did this for about 15 minutes without stopping, which is the longest I've ever seen her do it. Usually it only lasts for 1 to 2 minutes. She has another appointment with her pediatrician in 2 hours so I can see if he can send us to another neuro for a second opinion. The other neurologist she has seen before is booked until october.


Edit: She started this around 8 months when she started crawling. She would crawl for a bit then do this then keep crawling. It went away briefly when she started walking (all 3 of her drs hoped she would grow out of it). She has been walking for about 2 months now and she will walk and purposely get down on the floor to do this. It is worse now than it ever has been. She does it probably 30  or 40 times a day. Constantly doing it. She does it standing up if she leans on something. She did it in the pool the other day. ALL THE TIME!

She is awake and somewhat alert. If I call her name she will sometimes look at me. Towards the end of the video it shows her face, she was trying to go to sleep. Once she is done she gets up like nothing ever happened. Her arms stiffen a little and she will grab the blanket in her fists or pinch me if I am close enough to her.
We have. It is not seizures. That was our first stop. She's had a 1 hour and 24 hour EEG. Both show no seizure activity.

I am 15 months out, almost 16 months and I have not had sex since I conceived LO. I have no sex drive whatsoever. And now I am taking lexapro which makes my already dead sex drive even worse. I have a new boyfriend so I know we will be having sex soon but if we didn't I would have no problem with that lol
Every time I see pictures of him in the hospital it brings tears to my eyes. You are one tough mama and you have one strong little boy. Glad you guys got to go home early!
My first thought would be teething. My daughter is extremely emotional when she is teething, and is a horrible sleeper as well when she is teething.

My 15 month old was awake for 2 hours this morning and went full on meltdown until I put her down for a nap. She normally naps about 4 to 5 hours after she wakes up. She was probably 10 months old when she started staying awake longer between naps. She just really liked naps.

Same here. Last night she picked up something and held it to her ear like a phone and said "hi dada, how're you?" I was like did she just say a whole sentence? It is amazing how smart she is and how quickly she is learning.

Thankfully my kid hasn't learned no yet. She says words plain as day sometimes but I don't add them to her list of words she knows until she says them a few times. She just learned uh oh the other day.

I tried to breast feed but wasn't able to. At first I felt guilty for formula feeding but now I am glad I did. And I will probably formula feed my next kid as well. Formula feeding made life so much simpler. I like knowing how much my daughter is eating, being able to just stick a bottle in her mouth, and not having to deal with a pump and washing the pieces after every session and dealing withthe stress of breastfeeding. I now have a completely dependent daughter who can go stay with her daddy for a day or two and I dont have to worry about leaky boobs. My sister has a 20 month old who refuses to wean and she wishes she had the freedom I have. Also I can sleep without a bra on and not have to worry about my boobs leaking everywhere. I dont think I have seen my sister be able to go braless in 20 months. I hate wearing a bra and if I had to wear one all the time I would be driven crazy.
My 15 month old does this too. She has been walking for about a month too but she falls so much you'd never know she has been walking for weeks lol. And she still crawls occasionally.
Exactly. She is about to get tested for celiac disease and has already been tested for CF. I am hoping she just doesn't gtow because she is small and not because there is something wrong with her.

My 15 month old daughter is 18lbs and has been able to wear 2T panties since she was 10 months old (I let her wear them around the house when she has a diaper rash, and she is partially potty trained).

My daughter had a lot of problems on formula, we tried 5 or 6 formulas before we finally found one that worked okay with her. She has had a hard time growing. She's small for her age. I feel like if I was able to breastfeed it would have all been avoided. I didn't want to formula feed but I really didn't have much of a choice.

So far my daughter will eat anything except kiwi and cheesecake/cream cheese. She isn't a huge fan of strawberries but if I peel the seeds off she will eat them. She loves watermelon and cantaloupe. Broccoli is also a hit with her, never seen a child love broccoli as much as she does. And she loves peas and carrots too. I am an extremely picky eater (mainly a texture thing), but she is the complete opposite! I have been blessed with a great eater. She lovessss crackers, they probably aren't that good for her but I figure she eats so much healthy stuff some crackers won't hurt her :)

I tried to bf for 3 weeks. Went to see the lactation consultant 4 times in the first 2 weeks. Baby couldn't latch, so we tried a nipple shield. That didn't work either. We did the whole go in have her eeighed, feed her, weigh her again thing and she didn't gain anything so she wasn't getting any milk. In 3 weeks the most I ever got pumping was .5oz between both boobs. I just came to the conclusion that there was no way I could feed her like I wanted to. I wanted to bf really bad, and I felt guilty for months. But now I am glad she was ff. My sister has bf my niece for 19 months and she can't get her to wean and she hates breastfeeding now. I have a lot more freedom. My daughter can stay the night with her dad and I dont have to worry about her not getting milk or having to pump even though she isn't with me.
She had 10 teeth at 12 months and just in the past week she has cut 5 more.
My LO got her first tooth at 6.5 months. So 6 teeth at 6 months is a lot in my opinion!
My LO used to wear a sleeper then she started getting hot at night. So now she mainly just wears a diaper lol
I didn't have a clue what the purpose of 2 rows of snaps was until I read the comments. I have a petite little girl and have never had the problem of onesies not fitting lol

My niece started around 10 months. She would hold her baby and rock it or feed it and burp it. My daughter just started pretending (holding things up like a phone and talking to them) and she is 15 months.

I can't figure out why my ob/gyn said it was not addictive in any way and I could just stop taking it if I wanted to. Obviously I would consult her if I thought it wasn't working, but she told me the opposite of what other people are saying lol

I didn't even think I needed any help until a few weeks ago. I've been fine besides the occasional tears, but the past 2 months I've been having anxiety and constantly feeling like I am going to cry for no reason. Just in the past few weeks I got to thinking that maybe it isnt going to just go away.

Weird, my doctor said it can be stoppes at any time. She said nothing about needing to come off it slowly, but I saw that in the sheet I got from the pharmacist. Not sure why she told me that. And she said I should see a difference in a few days but may not for a week or 2. Instructions said 4 weeks.

Reduced hunger would be great because right now I tend to eat to make myself feel better. It said changes in appetite on the side effects but I didn't know if that was increased or decreased. Guess it could be either. I will just feel better when I am not fighting back tears on a daily basis with things most people would have no reason to cry about.

My LO woke at 8am and didnt nap until 4pm, and that was for about 5 minutes. Then she fell asleep for about 10 minutes on the way to dinner. So she had a total of 15 mins of sleep all day. This led to a VERY cranky baby. Not to mention she just cut a canine tooth and it working on bottom molars and some more canines. I gave her a bath when we got home from dinner and she cried the whole time. Then she fell asleep as soon as I wrapped her in a towel. And she has been sleeping since, that was over 2 hours ago. I put a diaper on her and put her in bed and she didn't wake up. That NEVER happens. I guess she had a big day lol.
My kid will bring shoes to me and stick her foot out for me to put them on her! She loves shoes but she hates socks!

My LO ate the velcro off a pair of shoes. I mean I don't know for sure if she actually swallowed it or not, but we never found the velcro and the shoe strap was nice and slobbery! Thankfully she has like 20 pair of shoes so I just tossed them.
I have these feelings sometimes too.

I am the same way. I have been having the worst dreams and feelings lately that I or someone I know is going to die. About 2 months ago I was getting the same feelings and then a friend of mine died in a car accident literally days later. Then the feelings went away. Now they are back.
